paper_title: More Tokens, Lower Precision Towards the Optimal Token-Precision   Trade-off in KV Cache Compression
caption: The results of layer-wise quantized pruning on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, with SnapKV as pruning method. We use 4 KV token 4-bit as baseline and report the relative change. Configurations are modified every 4 layers for the initial and final layers, while intermediate layers are reconfigured every 8 layers.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relative change in performance for different configurations of Llama-3-8B-Instruct following layer-wise quantized pruning. The x-axis represents the layer number and is scaled linearly from 1 to 32, with tick labels indicating Layer1-4, Layer5-12, Layer13-20, Layer21-28, and Layer29-32. The y-axis represents the relative change in performance, ranging from -15% to 5%, with tick marks spaced every 1% increment. The first line, colored orange and represented by circular markers, corresponds to LB-Avg of 2×tokens, 8-bit, displaying a consistent value around -2%, with a minimum value of -6% at Layer13-20 and a maximum value of -2% at Layer1-4. The second line, colored red and represented by circular markers, represents LB-Avg of 1×tokens, 16-bit, also exhibiting a consistent value around -3%, with a minimum value of -9% at Layer13-20 and a maximum value of -3% at Layer1-4. The third line, colored blue and represented by circular markers, represents RULER4k of 2×tokens, 8-bit, showing a value ranging from -5% to 0%, with a minimum of -12% at Layer13-20 and a maximum of 0% at Layer1-4. Finally, the fourth line, colored teal and represented by dashed markers, represents RULER4k of 1×tokens, 16-bit, with a value consistently around -4%, exhibiting a minimum of -10% at Layer13-20 and a maximum of -4% at Layer1-4, while a dashed line representing the baseline of 4×tokens, 4-bit, is present across all layers with a value of 0%.
